title: Basel Foundation — a playable design course
description: A playable foundation year in eight studios, in the spirit of the Basel School of Design's foundation program: point-line-plane compositions with live balance, density, rhythm and tension readouts and seeded variations; memory drawing scored by overlap (IoU); a draggable 1-, 2- and 3-point perspective playground; optical letter spacing with an area model and a stroke-contrast study; golden-angle seed heads and leaf venation from observed to abstract; generative hatching, stipple, weave and grain; seamless straight, half-drop and brick repeats; and colour studies in OKLCH. Each studio has a crit that reads your numbers back, and everything collects onto a printable A4 portfolio you can save as SVG or PNG. All exercises, text and images are original.
prompt: Build Basel Foundation, a playable design course: a fun, beautiful, interactive foundation year in the spirit of the Basel School of Design's foundation program as documented in Manfred Maier's Basic Principles of Design (1977). The book is in copyright, so don't reproduce or closely paraphrase any of its text, plates or exercises; everything must be original, and the footer should credit the program and the book and link the Internet Archive lending record. Use a Swiss / International Typographic Style: strict grid, flush-left type, white space, black and white with one or two accents, numbered sections, system fonts. Make eight studios, each with a short original principle, a 'try this' prompt and a crit panel that gives feedback from the measured values: point-line-plane compositions with balance, density, rhythm and tension readouts, presets and seeded variations; memory drawing shown for 3 seconds and scored by IoU; a 1-, 2- and 3-point perspective playground with draggable vanishing points and horizon; an optical letter-spacing game compared with an area model, plus a weight and contrast study; phyllotaxis and leaf venation from realistic to geometric; generative textures; straight, half-drop and brick textile repeats with seamless edges; and colour (simultaneous contrast with a reveal, an OKLCH value scale, proportion, warm and cool). Add a portfolio sheet that prints on A4 and downloads as SVG or PNG. Tests should check the centroid maths independently, IoU against a hand-computed case under page.clock, collinearity with the vanishing points, golden-angle positions, seamless repeats pixel for pixel, that the contrast swatches really are identical, print CSS, the credit and determinism per seed.

methodology: Independent geometry oracles: the composition measures are recomputed in the test from the rect and circle attributes actually drawn in the SVG (area-weighted centroid, nearest-neighbour rhythm, distance-to-edge tension), plus a hand case: a square and a dot on one row must put the centroid at (0.64·0.5 + π·0.16·11.5) / (0.64 + π·0.16). The perspective test reads every drawn edge and the handle positions, and requires each receding edge to pass through its vanishing point to within 1e-6 px in all three modes, before and after moving handles with the keyboard.

Hand-computed and published values: memory drawing uses a planted 7-cell target and a redraw with 5 shared cells out of a union of 9 (IoU 5/9), shown for exactly 3000 ms under page.clock. The golden angle is derived in the test as 360(1 − 1/φ), and at full abstraction all 300 seeds must sit on r = c√k, θ = kα. The contrast grey is checked against linear sRGB = L³ for an achromatic OKLCH colour, and each in-gamut step of the OKLCH scale is compared with Chrome's own oklch() conversion drawn on a canvas.

Pixel proofs where pixels matter: for each repeat type the pattern canvas must map onto itself under both lattice vectors (taken from the definition of straight, half-drop and brick, not from the page), and must equal the motif stamped continuously across the plane, pixel for pixel. The contrast SVG is rasterised through an Image and both swatches are sampled on each set of grounds.

Lettering is tested by reasoning, not snapshots: pairs of full-height stems (M, I, N) must keep the reference gap exactly, A's sloping sides must close their gaps, A–V must need a negative gap, and after 'Use model' the shoelace areas of the drawn red gap outlines must all be equal.

Output checks: print is emulated with emulateMedia and must hide everything except a 190 × 277 mm sheet with eight loaded images; the downloaded SVG must parse, be 794 × 1123, contain eight studio groups and no network hrefs; the PNG must have a valid signature and be 1588 × 2246. Determinism is checked with generate(seed) and by comparing the texture SVG and pattern canvas across reloads and seeds.
risks: The crit texts are rules of thumb built on my own simple measures (for example tension as the mean closeness to an edge, or temperature as a cosine of the OKLCH hue); they are not validated perceptual models, and the page describes them in general terms.
The spacing model is one reasonable area rule (depth capped at 30 units, reference = 1.2 × stem + 4); a trained letterer may disagree with it on individual pairs, and the page invites that.
The textile motif is rasterised in JavaScript with 4 × 4 supersampling rather than with canvas paths, so its edges are slightly softer than native anti-aliasing.
Colour appearance depends on the display; the tests prove the swatch values are identical, not how they look on a given screen.
qa.playwright: page.clock.install before goto plus pauseAt and runFor(2999)/runFor(1) pinned the memory drawing's three-second reveal exactly, and the redraw time reads 4.2 s because the clock was advanced 4200 ms. Most other tests read the rendered DOM (SVG attributes, canvas getImageData) and compute their own answer inside page.evaluate, so the oracle is separate from the page's model. emulateMedia({ media: 'print' }) tested the print CSS without a print dialog, and waitForEvent('download') captured both portfolio files for checks on disk. Keyboard focus and arrow keys drive the perspective handles, so the same test runs on desktop and on the touch Pixel 7 project. The textile test caught a real problem: canvas paths drawn at different absolute positions anti-alias differently in Chromium (a 44-level difference at the tile edges), so a tiled pattern never matched the continuous reference. Padding the canvas didn't fix it; rasterising the motif in tile-local integer coordinates did, and the test now demands zero differing pixels. The lettering test also caught a real bug: M's and N's diagonals poked past their stems at the top, which gave a straight-to-straight pair a non-reference gap.
coverage: Composition metrics vs a DOM oracle, hand centroid case, readouts and centroid mark
Crit wording, presets, keyboard placement, seeded variations
Memory: 3 s reveal under page.clock, IoU 5/9, timing, crit
Perspective collinearity in 1-, 2- and 3-point after handle moves; construction toggle
Lettering: reference gaps, negative A–V gap, equal shoelace areas, weight readout
Golden angle, Vogel positions, Fibonacci spirals, off-golden crit
Seamless repeats: lattice invariance and continuous-motif equality for all three types
Identical contrast swatches (DOM and raster), OKLCH scale vs the browser
Print CSS A4 sheet; SVG and PNG downloads
Footer credit and Archive link; determinism per seed

a11y: Every control is a native button, select or labelled range, and toggles use aria-pressed. The composition and memory grids are focusable, with a visible cursor: arrow keys move it and Enter places or removes an element. The perspective handles are focusable sliders that move with the arrow keys. Readouts, statuses and every crit are in aria-live regions, and each drawing has an aria-label that describes its current state in words. The portfolio images carry alt text with each studio's numbers.
